dz.headline: Algerian Minister Pledges Full State Support for Farmers After Fires
dz.dek: The agriculture minister visited affected areas in Jijel to assess damage and promised comprehensive state compensation for all agricultural losses.
paragraphs: Algeria's Minister of Agriculture, Rural Development, and Fisheries, Sid Ali Khaldi, visited Jijel province on Thursday to survey the damage caused by recent forest fires. The minister's visit focused on assessing the impact on farmers, livestock breeders, and their agricultural operations in the affected municipalities of Ouled Yahya Khadrouch and Bouraoui Belhadf.

During his visit, the minister met with local residents and assured them of the state's commitment to fully support those affected by the fires, regardless of the scale of their losses. He stated that the agriculture sector has mobilized all human and logistical resources to accurately count and evaluate the damages.

The assessment is a precursor to compensation and the swift resumption of agricultural activities. The support will extend to all individuals who lost livestock, facilities, or agricultural equipment due to the fires. The ministry aims to expedite the process of rebuilding and recovery for the affected communities.

dz.headline: Algeria Plans Regional Hub for African Medicine Supply
dz.dek: An Algerian meeting with UN agencies discussed establishing a regional center to supply essential medicines produced locally across Africa.
paragraphs: Algeria is moving forward with plans to establish a regional center for supplying essential medicines produced locally. Minister of Pharmaceutical Industry Wassim Guédri met with representatives from UNICEF, the World Health Organization, and UNIDO to discuss international cooperation in this area. This initiative follows a technical mission to Copenhagen in July to study the project and aims to bolster pharmaceutical production and health security on the continent.

The proposed center is a direct outcome of the African Ministerial Conference on Local Production of Medicines held in Algiers in November 2025. The conference resulted in the "Algiers Declaration," which outlines several initiatives to enhance cooperation among African nations in local drug manufacturing. Participants emphasized the need for a joint roadmap and a shared work calendar for 2026-2027 to begin supplying African markets with Algerian-produced essential medicines.

The meeting concluded with a call to strengthen strategic partnerships between Algeria and its international collaborators. The focus remains on translating the ministerial conference's outcomes into tangible projects and initiatives. This effort is intended to reinforce Algeria's role in supporting continental health security and promoting integration within the pharmaceutical industry across Africa.

dz.headline: Mohand Bouraï Assumes Central Bank Governor Role
dz.dek: Mohand Bouraï officially took over as the new governor of the Bank of Algeria, succeeding Mohamed Lamine Loukal.
paragraphs: Mohand Bouraï assumed his duties as the new governor of the Bank of Algeria on Thursday, September 3. He replaces Mohamed Lamine Loukal, who was appointed Minister of Finance in the recent partial cabinet reshuffle. The handover ceremony was overseen by the outgoing governor and now Minister of Finance, Mohamed Lamine Loukal.

During the ceremony, Bouraï stated that Algerian banks possess sufficient liquidity and that the financing of the economy is experiencing notable growth. He indicated that the central bank is committed to supporting economic expansion through adequate financial resources.

The appointment of Bouraï marks a transition in the leadership of Algeria's central bank. His initial remarks suggest a focus on maintaining financial stability and encouraging economic development through robust banking sector liquidity and credit provision.

dz.headline: Algeria Postpones National Quran Week
dz.dek: The Ministry of Religious Affairs and Endowments announced the postponement of the 28th edition of the National Quranic Week, originally set to begin September 7, 2026.
paragraphs: Algeria's Ministry of Religious Affairs and Endowments announced on Thursday the postponement of the 28th edition of the National Quranic Week. The event was scheduled to commence on September 7, 2026, but has now been rescheduled to an unspecified later date.

The ministry stated that the new date for the Quranic Week will be announced in due course. They reiterated their hope that the occasion will serve as a blessed time for gathering around the Holy Book and celebrating its adherents. The previous edition of the National Quranic Week was held in the state of Boumerdes, starting September 15, 2025.

The Quranic Week typically includes national competitions for memorization and recitation of the Quran, alongside academic seminars and other activities. The postponement affects the planned schedule for these cultural and religious events across the country.

These services aim to expand digital offerings and enhance inter-sectoral interoperability, following directives from the President.

The new services include applications for connecting to the potable water network, allowing citizens to submit and track requests remotely. Another service enables online submission and tracking of applications for connection to the public sewage network, with electronic processing of requests.

The third service caters to businesses in the water sector, facilitating the submission, management, and tracking of applications for professional qualification and classification certificates. The High Commission indicated that more digital services will be introduced on the portal in the future.

ao.headline: Angola Opens Two Dams to Combat Drought Effects in Cunene
ao.dek: The Calucuve and Ndúe dams, part of a program to fight drought in southern Angola, are set to open after nearly five years of construction.
paragraphs: President João Lourenço is scheduled to inaugurate the Calucuve and Ndúe dams in the Cuvelai municipality of Cunene province this Friday. These two structures are key components of the Program to Combat the Effects of Drought in Southern Angola (PCESSA). The dams are intended to supply water for consumption, agricultural irrigation, and livestock, addressing a long-standing issue of water scarcity that has historically driven migration to Namibia.

The Ndúe dam will initially serve approximately fifty-five thousand inhabitants and sixty thousand head of cattle, with a storage capacity of one hundred seventy million cubic meters of water and a seventy-five-kilometer aqueduct. The Calucuve dam will benefit around eighty thousand inhabitants and nearly two hundred thousand head of cattle, holding one hundred forty-one million cubic meters of water. These projects aim to mitigate the impacts of recurrent droughts, exacerbated by El Niño, which have severely affected provinces like Cunene, Huíla, and Namibe.

The inauguration follows nearly five years of construction and adds to the existing Cafu canal. According to the MPLA news agency Angop, these dams are considered structuring projects for drought resilience in the region. Amnesty International's latest report highlights the dire conditions faced by thousands of Angolans who have crossed into Namibia due to lack of water for both personal use and economic activities over past decades.

ao.headline: UNITA Returns to Uíge for Pre-Election Meeting
ao.dek: The opposition party will convene its Standing Committee to prepare for the 2027 general elections, marking a return after a prior event was disrupted.
paragraphs: UNITA has returned to Uíge, Angola, to hold a Standing Committee meeting on Friday in preparation for the 2027 general elections. Party president Adalberto Costa Júnior stated the visit aims to conclude an "incomplete journey" referencing an August 8 incident where police dispersed UNITA youth members and a planned tribute to founder Jonas Savimbi was postponed.

Costa Júnior recalled that UNITA members left Uíge on August 9 without police escort, deeming it untrustworthy after the previous day's events. He noted their arrival was met with a positive reception and expressed hope for a similar departure, with a planned return to Luanda on Saturday. The party leader emphasized the necessity of their return to reaffirm the democratic rule of law.

The UNITA leader asserted that the state belongs to all Angolans and is a plural entity. The party's return to Uíge is intended to demonstrate their commitment to political processes and to ensure a peaceful environment for their activities, contrasting with the previous disruption.

ao.headline: Angolan Tax Authority Trains Staff on Financial Crimes
ao.dek: The Angolan Tax Authority (AGT) is enhancing its capacity to combat tax fraud, money laundering, and corruption through a specialized training program.
paragraphs: The Angolan Tax Authority (AGT) has launched a training initiative focused on "Tax Fraud, Money Laundering, and Corruption: Who, Where, and How?" The program, developed in cooperation with the Attorney General's Office of Angola, aims to equip tax officials with advanced knowledge to identify and address financial crimes.

Noémia Ido, speaking at the training's commencement, highlighted that tax crimes are often interconnected with other offenses, particularly money laundering. She noted that issues related to income tax retention, where companies collect but do not remit taxes to the state, and Value Added Tax (VAT) collection irregularities are common.

AGT Chairman José Leiria emphasized the importance of coordinated action between tax bodies and investigative agencies. Attorney General Pedro Mendes de Carvalho added that tackling economic and financial crime requires technical preparation and robust institutional cooperation to strengthen the state's revenue collection and national reputation.

ao.headline: Children Undertake Pilgrimage to Muxima Sanctuary
ao.dek: Two thousand children from various parishes gathered at Angola's largest Marian devotion sanctuary for a day of faith and spiritual learning.
paragraphs: Two thousand children from different parish communities of the Diocese undertook a pilgrimage to the Municipality of Quiçama, Icolo and Bengo province, specifically to the town of Muxima. The event, held at the largest sanctuary of Marian devotion in sub-Saharan Africa, aimed to provide a journey of encounter with God and devotion to the patroness. Dressed in parish colors and symbols, the children experienced an atmosphere of joy and enthusiasm during the event.

During the homily, Bishop Emílio Sumbelelo encouraged the children to live with sincerity and make truth a fundamental principle, urging them not to fear speaking truthfully and to grow committed to Christian values. He shared personal childhood memories to connect with the young attendees. The Bishop expressed a wish for future pilgrimages to include children from all Angolan dioceses, aiming to make the gathering a national event of faith and communion.

For the participating children, the pilgrimage offered an opportunity to absorb the Bishop's teachings. Gabriel de Moura, Aninho Fernandes, and Natividade Pacheco stated they understood the message and were willing to follow the advice, particularly the call to always tell the truth. The event concluded with a visit to the sanctuary and leisure time, marking a significant moment for the Diocese of Viana's childhood ministry.

bj.headline: Benin President Mediates Celestial Church Dispute
bj.dek: Former President Patrice Talon, now Senate President, is working to ease tensions within the Celestial Church of Christ and announced upcoming legislation on religious.
paragraphs: Hundreds gathered on August 29th in Saint-Ouen, near Paris, for an information meeting organized by the France diocese of the Church of Celestial Christianity. The unexpected guest at this religious forum was Patrice Talon, the former head of state of Benin and current President of the Senate. His presence signals a high-level engagement in resolving internal disputes within the church.

Talon's intervention comes after a significant step towards reconciliation within the Church of Celestial Christ. On April 30, 2026, he received the final report from the Superior Council of Transition at the Sofitel Cotonou Marina, a process aimed at healing divisions. This involvement suggests a continued effort by the former president to influence the political landscape through religious mediation.

The former president's actions indicate a desire to maintain a role in national affairs by addressing sensitive internal church matters. The announcement of a forthcoming law on the organization of worship in Benin, made during his address in the Paris region, is seen as a strategic move to manage religious affairs and potentially consolidate his influence.

bj.headline: African Russian cultural centers face private management amid sanctions
bj.dek: State agency Rossotrudnichestvo's assets are frozen by the EU, leading to externalized management of Russian cultural centers in Africa.
paragraphs: The European Union has frozen the financial assets of Rossotrudnichestvo, the Russian state agency overseeing cultural centers worldwide, since July 2022. This measure aimed to disrupt Moscow's public diplomacy tools abroad. Despite these sanctions, some centers, like the one in Paris, continue their operations, offering language courses and cultural events.

Several European governments have unilaterally terminated agreements with local Russian cultural centers. Romania closed its center in February 2023, followed by Denmark and Moldova, which is set to close its Chisinau branch in July 2026. Germany formally ended bilateral agreements due to suspected intelligence activities.

Investigations reveal that some Russian cultural centers in Africa are now managed by private entities. These centers are reportedly used as geopolitical influence tools and recruitment channels, operating outside the European Union's direct financial oversight.

bj.headline: Congo Teachers Demand Back Pay, Threaten School Year Start
bj.dek: Twelve thousand community teachers in Congo-Brazzaville are demanding ten months of unpaid allowances and threaten a general strike if not paid.
paragraphs: Approximately twelve thousand community teachers in Congo-Brazzaville are demanding payment of their outstanding allowances. These educators, who support the national education system without civil servant status, insist on receiving their back pay before the upcoming school year begins. The teachers have accumulated a deficit of ten months of unpaid allowances from the Congolese state.

To ensure a peaceful school reopening and avoid disruptions, the protesting teachers have set a condition: at least four months of their owed sums must be settled before they return to classrooms. They organized a protest in the capital, Brazzaville, in front of the National Institute for Pedagogical Research and Action, under the banner of the Coalition of Community Teacher Structures of Congo (CSECC).

Beyond financial demands, the protesters criticize the authorities' proposed conditions for permanent employment, rejecting the requirement for a competitive exam for public service integration. The CSECC argues that their years of experience justify direct integration. If their demands regarding allowances and recruitment are not met, the community teachers plan to initiate a general strike at the start of October 2026.

bw.headline: Parliament Approves National Health Insurance Policy
bw.dek: Lawmakers unanimously adopted the policy on August 19, paving the way for a ten-year partnership with Abu Dhabi Health Data Services.
paragraphs: Botswana's Parliament has unanimously adopted the National Health Insurance Policy, marking a significant step towards its implementation. The policy, approved on August 19, aims to ensure equitable access to quality healthcare for all citizens, regardless of their location or income.

Following the policy's adoption, the Ministry of Health announced a decade-long partnership with Abu Dhabi Health Data Services (ADHDS). This collaboration will focus on improving the supply chain for medicines and medical products, alongside broader health system enhancements, including digital health initiatives and genomics.

Minister of Health Dr. Stephen Modise has emphasized that the National Health Insurance scheme is fundamentally about dignity and equity. The partnership with ADHDS is expected to bolster the health system's capacity to deliver on this promise, addressing previous concerns about medicine shortages by focusing on evidence-based solutions and system-wide cooperation.

bw.headline: Botswana Government Seeks P30 Billion Bond Ceiling Increase
bw.dek: Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe asks Parliament to raise the government bond issuance ceiling to P85 billion, citing financing flexibility.
paragraphs: Parliament has been asked to approve an increase in Botswana's government bond issuance ceiling from P55 billion to P85 billion. Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe stated that the proposed P30 billion rise is intended to provide greater flexibility in financing government operations, rather than indicating an immediate plan to borrow the full amount. The ceiling represents the maximum value of government securities that can be outstanding at any given time.

Gaolathe emphasized that the proposed higher ceiling should not be misconstrued as a borrowing target or an intention to utilize the entire sum. The move aims to ensure the government has adequate room to manage its financial obligations and potential future needs without immediate constraints. This adjustment is a procedural step to accommodate potential market conditions and financing requirements.

The request to raise the bond issuance ceiling is currently before Parliament for consideration. The minister's explanation focuses on the strategic financial management aspect of the proposal, assuring legislators that the increase is a proactive measure for flexibility. The ultimate decision rests with the parliamentary body on whether to approve the revised ceiling.

bf.headline: Minister Simporé Honors Sankara, Urges Youth to Build Nation
bf.dek: The Minister of War and Patriotic Defense presided over the 11th monthly military ceremony honoring Thomas Sankara and his companions.
paragraphs: General of Division Célestin Simporé, Minister of War and Patriotic Defense, led the 11th monthly military ceremony at the Thomas Sankara Memorial on September 3, 2026. The event, attended by ministry personnel, honored President Thomas Sankara and his companions, emphasizing their ideals of dignity, sovereignty, and social justice. Simporé stated that Sankara's memory calls for reflection on collective responsibilities and the nation's destiny, free from dependency.

The ceremony, marked by military music and protocol, underscored Sankara's commitment to human rights, women's emancipation, education, health, and anti-corruption efforts. Minister Simporé highlighted that Sankara's values serve as a guide for public policy and daily life. He also acknowledged the dedication of all Burkinabè citizens, including defense and security forces, civil servants, educators, healthcare workers, farmers, and civil society members, recognizing their efforts as the nation's true strength.

Simporé specifically addressed the youth, emphasizing their crucial role in national construction. He urged them to embrace the ideals of the Revolution and actively participate in building the country. The event also included discussions in Passoré province on the ideological foundations of the Popular Progressive Revolution, leadership, and youth responsibilities in consolidating Sahel states, aiming to foster engagement and understanding among young people and the wider community.

bf.headline: Nahouri officials review agro-pastoral gains and challenges
bf.dek: Local leaders met in Pô to assess the 2026-2027 agricultural campaign and the 2023-2026 agro-pastoral offensive's progress.
paragraphs: Members of the technical committee and general assembly of the Provincial Council for Food Security (CT-CPSA) convened in Pô on September 3, 2026. The meeting focused on the 2026-2027 agro-pastoral campaign, the food and nutritional situation, and the 2023-2026 agro-pastoral and fishing offensive's contribution to food sovereignty in the Nahouri province.

The session, themed "From the 2023-2026 Agro-Pastoral and Fishing Offensive to Food Sovereignty in Nahouri Province: Gains, Challenges, and Prospects," aimed to review local progress and identify obstacles hindering production. Provincial Director of Agriculture for Nahouri, Aïcha Sanou/Zidwemba, highlighted the council as a vital tool for local governance, fostering dialogue and synergy among stakeholders for food and nutritional security.

Participants reaffirmed their commitment to national strategies for sustainable food self-sufficiency. Discussions covered advancements made within the province and pinpointed difficulties affecting agricultural output. The meeting underscored the importance of local collaboration in addressing food security and nutritional challenges.

bf.headline: Youth Launch Resilience Tournament in Piéla
bf.dek: Six teams from Piéla are competing in a football tournament aimed at strengthening community ties and promoting peace.
paragraphs: The youth of Piéla officially launched the "Maracana of resilience and social cohesion" on Sunday, a competition featuring six teams representing different parts of the commune. The initiative, spearheaded by Biyourpo Lankoandé, aims to foster closer relationships among residents and promote peace, solidarity, and coexistence amidst national security challenges.

The tournament emphasizes fair play, respect, solidarity, and unity, serving as more than just a sporting event. It provides a platform for fraternity, dialogue, and connection among the commune's youth. The six participating teams draw from various segments of Piéla's population, reflecting the organizers' goal of creating an inclusive and unifying space. The opening day saw FC Dortmund defeat FC Jeune Talent 2-0, while FC Privée and FC Folbongou drew 0-0.

Organizers and participants view each match as an opportunity to reinforce bonds within the community and champion peace and social cohesion, transcending the purely sporting results. This event highlights the role of sport in bridging divides and fostering a sense of shared identity in the region.

bf.headline: Culture professionals train with weapons at police academy
bf.dek: Twenty-one cultural professionals completed a voluntary patriotic immersion program that included firearms training.
paragraphs: Twenty-one cultural professionals participated in a voluntary patriotic immersion program, which included a live firing exercise at Badnoogo on Thursday, September 3, 2026. The participants familiarized themselves with handling weapons, including RPG7s, machine guns, and Kalashnikovs, at the National Police Special Intervention Group (GSIPN) training center. They received briefings on the assembly, disassembly, and operation of various military-grade firearms.

The GSIPN commander, Issa Zongo, commended the participants for their voluntary engagement and expressed pride in their willingness to learn about weaponry. The training, a partnership between the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of Security, involved 25 cultural actors from August 20 to September 4, 2026, at the police academy. Marius Diessongo, representing the trainees, described the experience as one of stress management and self-transcendence, yielding satisfactory results.

The immersion program aimed to instill patriotic values and practical skills. Participants engaged in theoretical and practical sessions, culminating in the firearms training. This initiative is part of a broader effort to foster a new generation of integrated and patriotic Burkinabè citizens committed to national development and sovereignty.

bf.headline: Amon Bazongo Builds AI Ecosystems Linking Burkina Faso and Asia
bf.dek: Technology entrepreneur Amon Bazongo is fostering innovation by connecting Burkina Faso with Asian tech hubs and developing AI applications.
paragraphs: Amon Bazongo, a technology entrepreneur and artificial intelligence consultant, is bridging Burkina Faso with Asian innovation hubs. Bazongo, who grew up with digital technology, sees AI, blockchain, and big data as new frontiers for learning and entrepreneurship. He believes technological revolutions only have real impact when an ecosystem forms around them, emphasizing training, connection, and community building in his work.

Bazongo's academic journey began in Burkina Faso with an electrical and electronics engineering degree from the University Polytechnique of Bobo-Dioulasso. He then pursued international studies in Taiwan, earning degrees in computer science and Big Data Management. His professional career started in Taiwan, developing marketing applications and chatbots. He later transitioned to AI consulting, notably working on inCare, an AI system for cardiology developed with a Kaohsiung hospital.

His work on inCare highlights his approach to AI as a practical tool for strategic sectors like healthcare. Bazongo's career trajectory is now increasingly focused on the digital transformation challenges facing the African continent. He is recognized as one of the 100 personalities shaping Burkina Faso's digital landscape, contributing to a generation that views emerging technologies as opportunities for development.

bi.headline: Man found stabbed in river, another beaten and left in woods
bi.dek: Two separate violent incidents in Gitega province have resulted in one man dead and another critically injured, with police arresting suspects in both cases.
paragraphs: A 60-year-old man, identified as Marc Nzikobanyanka, was discovered dead in the Kanyangwa river on Wednesday morning. Witnesses suggest he was stabbed before his body was placed in the water. The exact motive for the killing remains unknown, though authorities are investigating the possibility of a robbery linked to three million Burundian francs he recently withdrew after selling coffee. Two individuals, Jean Bosco Ndayishimiye and Levis Nimbona, have been arrested as part of the ongoing investigation.

In a separate incident, a 38-year-old man, Claude Nahimana, was found in a comatose state, wrapped in bags and abandoned in an eucalyptus grove on Thursday morning. Local officials stated he had been severely beaten. A land dispute is being considered as a potential motive, but this has not been officially confirmed. Two men, Clovis Ntahimpera and Joël Nizigiyimana, have been apprehended by police for questioning.

These two cases add to a growing number of violent incidents in Gitega province. Since the beginning of 2026, over 90 individuals have been reported killed or found dead in the region. This tally includes cases reported from various sources, and not all circumstances have been definitively established. The province experienced a surge in fatalities in August, with approximately ten people dying or being found lifeless within a ten-day period.

bi.headline: Burundi Schools Charge Fees Despite Free Education Policy
bi.dek: Parents report being asked for payments for school supplies, repairs, and even admission, undermining the government's free fundamental education initiative.
paragraphs: Despite Burundi's policy of free fundamental education, parents in communes like Ntahangwa and Mukaza are still paying fees. One parent noted quarterly payments of three thousand FBu for a fifth-year student and thirteen thousand FBu for an eighth-year student, with explanations for these charges remaining unclear. Another parent paid twenty thousand FBu to secure a place for their child, a practice that contradicts the stated free enrollment for fundamental education.

The Provincial Directorate of Education in Bujumbura issued a directive on August sixth, 2026, reminding communal education department heads to enforce the strict respect of school enrollment instructions. The directive explicitly states that first-year fundamental students should not face any enrollment fees and prohibits forced financial contributions for items like desks or other admission-related conditions.

Jean Samandari, president of the Coalition Education for tous « Bafashebige », stated that while schools require resources for functioning, these financial shortfalls should not be passed to families. He advocates for increased public funding, better governance, and transparency in any requested contributions, emphasizing that free education must be a reality, not just a principle, and that family financial difficulties should not hinder a child's schooling.

bi.headline: Burundi President Offers Cash Reward for Youth Informants
bi.dek: A presidential decree offers 500 million Burundian francs to young ruling party members who report arsonists, raising questions about security duties.
paragraphs: Burundi's President has announced a substantial reward of 500 million Burundian francs for any young militant of the ruling party who catches and denounces an alleged arsonist. This sum is equivalent to several years of net salaries for police officers and other security agents tasked with safeguarding the nation. The announcement, intended to encourage citizens to report suspected arsonists, has been specifically directed towards the youth wing of the ruling party, the Imbonerakure.

The presidential call for vigilance, while framed within the constitutional duty of every Burundian to defend national independence and territorial integrity, has taken a specific turn by offering a financial incentive. Critics question whether this approach undermines the constitutional mandate of established security forces, suggesting it could lead to a sense of exclusion among those not affiliated with the ruling party and potentially devalue the work of official security personnel.

This policy raises concerns about whether peace and security are becoming exclusive domains for a select group, potentially discouraging official security bodies who may feel unappreciated. The significant financial reward, described as 'enormous' and 'tempting,' has sparked debate about the most effective ways to ensure public safety and whether strengthening existing security structures would be more beneficial than incentivizing a specific political faction.

bi.dek: A ruling party official indicated a willingness to examine tax exemptions for sanitary products after a journalist raised the issue.
paragraphs: A journalist questioned the Secretary General of the CNDD-FDD party on August 22, 2026, in Makamba, regarding the taxation of sanitary pads. The official, appearing surprised, turned to his colleagues and asked them to note the question for future discussion. This interaction highlights the ongoing debate about the accessibility of essential menstrual hygiene products in Burundi, where many families struggle with economic precarity.

Data from the NGO SaCoDé suggests that over 80% of Burundian women lack access to sanitary pads, with UNICEF Burundi reporting in 2021 that 83% of adolescent girls face precarious menstrual hygiene conditions, leading 70% to miss school during their periods. The current finance law for 2026/2027 does not offer specific exemptions for these products, subjecting them to general import taxes, which contribute to their final cost for consumers.

The government has previously used fiscal policy to support other sectors, such as electric vehicles, modern cooking equipment, and certified seeds, demonstrating its capacity to adapt tax measures for specific objectives. The question of whether menstrual hygiene products could receive similar consideration for tax relief is now on the table, potentially making them more accessible, particularly for low-income households.

bi.headline: Burundi Football Federation Renews WANAW Kit Deal
bi.dek: The FFB has extended its partnership with Ethiopian sportswear manufacturer WANAW for another year, citing improved team image and performance.
paragraphs: The Burundi Football Federation (FFB) has renewed its contract with Ethiopian sportswear maker WANAW for a second year. This decision, under the leadership of Brigadier General of Police Alexandre Muyenge, signifies a commitment to providing national teams, including the Intamba Mu Rugamba, U20, and U17 squads, with high-quality apparel. The federation views WANAW not just as a supplier but as a partner in building a stronger football ecosystem.

Over the past year, WANAW has supplied kits described as 'armor' that fit the players like a 'second skin,' meeting FIFA and CAF standards. This collaboration aims to enhance the image of Burundi's national teams, moving from a 'plea' to a 'banner' through modern, comfortable, and aesthetically regal designs. The FFB expressed gratitude to Habte Garment Printing for its consistency and support.

The FFB's renewed trust in WANAW is based on conviction rather than habit, reflecting a belief that footballing greatness is built incrementally. This alliance is part of the FFB's broader strategy to support its athletes with gear worthy of their efforts and to foster an environment where private partners actively contribute to development, not just financial backing.

cm.headline: Cameroon Ministry Invites SMEs to Indonesia Trade Expo
cm.dek: The Ministry of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises is seeking Cameroonian businesses to explore opportunities at the 41st Trade Expo Indonesia.
paragraphs: Cameroonian businesses are invited to participate in the 41st Trade Expo Indonesia 2026, scheduled for October 14-18 in Tangerang, near Jakarta. The Ministry of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises, Social Economy and Handicrafts (MINPMEESA) issued the invitation on August 31, targeting SME promoters, professional associations, and corporations interested in the Indonesian market. The event aims to connect international buyers with Indonesian exporters and suppliers.

Organized by Indonesia’s Ministry of Trade, the annual expo features exhibitions, business-matching sessions, trade missions, seminars, and official meetings. This year's exhibition will showcase five product zones: food, beverages and agriculture; manufactured goods; industrial estates; fashion and crafts; and furniture and home decor. Interested Cameroonian economic operators can register via the official Trade Expo Indonesia platform or contact the Indonesian Embassy in Yaounde.

The expo provides a platform for importers, exporters, manufacturers, investors, and trade institutions to engage. MINPMEESA's announcement encourages businesses to leverage this opportunity to explore potential trade and investment ventures in Indonesia. The event is designed to foster international business relationships and facilitate market access for participating companies.

cm.headline: Minister Orders Immediate Land Reform Implementation
cm.dek: Cameroon's Minister of State Property, Land Survey, and Land Affairs announced new directives for land governance, impacting consultative commissions and future legislation.
paragraphs: Yaoundé, Cameroon – Minister Henri Eyebe Ayissi on September 1, 2026, launched special sessions on land reform, mandating the immediate application of circular letters 2024-2026 and a new directive on consultative commissions. The minister cited demographic pressure, urbanization, and disputes as reasons for reform, aligning with national development strategies and FAO guidelines. He emphasized the need for updated records of traditional chiefdom attestations and adherence to new commission guidelines.

The reform aims to address the limitations of the 1974 ordinance, which has struggled to cope with current societal changes. Key announcements included the signing of Circular Letter No. 0005, detailing how notables will be appointed to consultative commissions. A rigorous parliamentary review of a future land law project was also promised. The minister stressed strict and immediate application of these new rules, including the submission of all ongoing cases to the updated regulations.

Administrative authorities, traditional leaders, and land sector stakeholders attended the meeting at the Regional Council of Centre. The minister's directives require an annual updated file of third-degree chiefdom attestations and updated commission descent scales. All current land dossiers must be processed under the new rules, with non-compliance potentially leading to sanctions.

cm.headline: Cameroon Treasury Debt Reaches CFA2 Trillion as Growth Slows
cm.dek: Cameroon's outstanding government securities on the CEMAC market reached CFA2.061 trillion by July 2026, marking a significant slowdown in annual growth to 4.1%.
paragraphs: Cameroon's total outstanding Treasury securities on the CEMAC public debt market surpassed CFA2 trillion by the end of July 2026. The stock reached CFA2.061 trillion, an increase of CFA80.4 billion, or 4.1%, from the previous year, according to Bank of Central African States statistics. This represents a sharp deceleration in growth compared to the preceding two years, which saw increases of 23.7% and 29.6% respectively.

The nation held the third-largest stock of government securities within the six-member CEMAC region, accounting for 19.5% of the total CFA10.561 trillion in outstanding securities. Gabon led the regional market with CFA3.424 trillion, followed by Congo with CFA3.041 trillion. Cameroon's debt stock grew by CFA293 billion between July 2023 and July 2024, and by CFA452.2 billion in the year prior to that.

The slowdown in the annual growth rate of Cameroon's outstanding Treasury securities indicates a shift from the rapid expansion observed in recent years. The figures, published by the Bank of Central African States, detail the country's position within the regional debt market and the recent trajectory of its government borrowing.

cm.headline: Cameroon Launches New Debt Audit Amid CFA288.8 Billion Unpaid Arrears
cm.dek: Finance Minister Louis Paul Motazé has directed government agencies to submit claims for an audit of unstructured debt accumulated between 2020 and 2025.
paragraphs: Cameroon has initiated a fresh audit to identify unpaid government obligations accumulated between 2020 and 2025. This new exercise proceeds despite CFA288.8 billion from a prior review remaining unsettled. The audit aims to quantify the extent of new debt accrued across various government entities over the specified six-year period.

In a directive dated August 19, 2026, Finance Minister Louis Paul Motazé mandated that all government agencies, public bodies, ministries, state universities, public institutions, companies, and local authorities submit their claims for the 2020-2025 period to the Directorate General of Budget by October 31. The review focuses on determining the volume of unstructured debt claimed against these entities since 2020.

The Finance Ministry defines floating debt as unstructured claims presented by third parties against the central government and its associated entities. The total amount can only be definitively established after all claims are identified, supporting documentation is scrutinized, and the figures are validated through a comprehensive audit process.

cm.headline: New EU Ambassador Presents Credentials in Yaoundé
cm.dek: Veronika Boskovic Pohar met with Felix Mbayu to discuss bilateral cooperation and Cameroon's socio-political situation.
paragraphs: Veronika Boskovic Pohar officially began her tenure as the new head of the European Union delegation to Cameroon on September 2, 2026, by presenting her letters of credence to the Ministry of External Relations in Yaoundé. She met with Felix Mbayu, the Minister Delegate for Cooperation with the Commonwealth, to review existing cooperation between Cameroon and the EU. The meeting also provided a platform to discuss the current socio-political climate within Cameroon.

Boskovic Pohar, a career diplomat, succeeds Jean Marc Châtaigner, whose mission concluded at the end of August. She expressed her commitment to working with Cameroonian authorities to achieve her mandate. Her extensive background includes twenty years of experience in security policy, multilateral relations, and EU foreign policy. Prior to her appointment in Cameroon, she served as the head of the EU delegation in Afghanistan from September 1, 2024.

Before her assignment in Afghanistan, Boskovic Pohar held significant roles within the EU's diplomatic corps. Between September 2020 and August 2024, she represented the Political and Security Committee at the EU's permanent representation in Slovenia. She also served as deputy head of the Slovenian mission in France and Morocco. A lawyer by training, the Slovenian diplomat was designated to lead the EU delegation in Cameroon three months prior to presenting her credentials.

cf.headline: Pediatric Center Sees Fewer Sick Children After Care Costs Return
cf.dek: Parents are avoiding the Bangui Pediatric Complex due to renewed medical fees, leading to empty beds and a drop in patient numbers.
paragraphs: The Bangui Pediatric Complex is experiencing a significant decrease in patient visits following the suspension of some free healthcare programs. Parents are now hesitant to bring their sick children due to the reintroduction of certain medical fees, with some opting for self-medication or local remedies. Waiting rooms are noticeably less crowded, and many beds in Units A and B remain empty, a stark contrast to previous attendance levels.

Previously, targeted free care for children under five, pregnant women, and nursing mothers, supported by partners since 2016, meant many families could access services without cost. However, the return of consultation, examination, and medication fees has created a barrier for those lacking financial means. The director of the complex, Professor Jean Chrysostome Gody, stated that the government maintains targeted free care, shifting from total to selective coverage for specific demographics, a policy implemented in early 2026.

Beyond the financial strain, parents also report dissatisfaction with the reception and waiting times at the facility. One user anonymously described a lengthy wait for medical attention, even after paying for a medical record. The director attributed these reception issues to a lack of civility, while health officials are appealing to authorities and partners for support amidst these challenges.

cf.headline: Miskine trial nears closing arguments in Chad
cf.dek: Central African leader Abdoulaye Miskine faces charges of insurrection, rape, and murder as his trial continues in N'Djamena.
paragraphs: The trial of Abdoulaye Miskine, leader of the Front démocratique pour le peuple centrafricain (FDPC), is set to resume on September 4 in N'Djamena, Chad, after a two-day suspension. Miskine and his co-accused face charges including creating an insurrectional movement, rape, assassination, and torture stemming from events in 2001 and 2002. The court has been hearing from civil parties and the accused, with chronological elements focusing on Miskine's alleged role in combating rebellion under President Ange-Félix Patassé.

Central African refugees from the Maro camp in Chad have requested to testify, aiming to provide evidence on crimes and violence attributed to Miskine's forces. Miskine's defense argues he was an official security commander fighting alongside the Central African army, not a rebel leader. The proceedings are scheduled to continue with the public prosecutor's arguments and pleas from the civil parties and the defense.

Miskine and three co-accused were arrested in southeastern Chad on November 19, 2019, and have been detained in N'Djamena for several years. Chadian authorities accuse them of creating an insurrectional movement, assassination, rape, torture, and sequestration. The Central African government's request for Miskine's extradition to Bangui has been unsuccessful.

cf.headline: Bees force UN humanitarian plane to land in Bambari
cf.dek: A United Nations humanitarian flight en route to Bangassou made an emergency landing in Bambari on Monday after bees swarmed the aircraft's cabin.
paragraphs: A United Nations humanitarian plane traveling from Bangui to Bangassou was forced to divert its flight and land in Bambari on Monday, August 31, 2026. The diversion occurred after several bees entered the aircraft's cabin while it was flying over the Ouaka region.

The incident happened shortly after the plane departed from Bangui-M'Poko airport. The pilot decided to land in Bambari to ensure the safety of the passengers and to allow for the removal of the insects from the cabin. No passengers were reported injured during the event.

Following the evacuation of all occupants, the bees were removed from the plane. The aircraft then underwent a thorough cleaning and disinfection process before it was cleared to continue its journey to Bangassou.

cf.headline: Farmer-herder clashes halt farming in Batangafo
cf.dek: Farmers abandon fields in Ouham-Fafa region due to armed herders, destroying crops and livestock amid ongoing tensions.
paragraphs: Tensions between farmers and armed herders have paralyzed agricultural activities in Batangafo, Ouham-Fafa. Farmers have fled their fields for several days, fearing the presence of armed herders who have devastated crops. This conflict, fueled by livestock destroying farms and herders' animals being killed, has resulted in over seven deaths and numerous injuries in the past three months.

The ongoing violence has forced residents like Madeleine Noukouma, a widow and mother of eleven, to abandon her farm in Diri village. She stated that the armed herders instilled fear, leading to their departure and the destruction of their livelihoods. Noukouma expressed a willingness to return if peace is restored and a solution is found.

Local authorities are attempting to de-escalate the situation. Fatimé Salet, president of the National Federation of Herders of CAR, urged herders to keep their cattle away from farmlands. Sub-prefect Robert Yekoua-Kette emphasized the need to respect the transhumance corridor and warned against cattle theft, while acknowledging the persistent fear among residents due to armed herders near the town.

cg.headline: Ministers Testify on Makotimpoko Border Clash
cg.dek: Congolese Defense and Interior ministers briefed lawmakers on an incident involving RDC forces and territorial disputes.
paragraphs: The Defense and Security Commission of the National Assembly heard testimony on August 31 and September 1 from the ministers of Defense and Interior regarding events in Makotimpoko. The hearings aimed to clarify the circumstances of an attack on public force agents by elements of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (RDC), the event's progression, and its casualties. Deputies also sought information on the legal status of disputed territories and border surveillance.

Defense Minister Raymond Zéphirin Mboulou presented colonial texts from 1908 to assert Congo's claim over territories like Mokoloko Island, acknowledging that some populations originate from the RDC. He described the Makotimpoko incidents as "regrettable" and condemned the broadcast of "humiliating" images, emphasizing the government's preference for diplomatic solutions and dialogue between the two nations.

Interior Minister Jean Olessongo Ondaye welcomed the parliamentary commission's initiative, stating it clarified misunderstandings and the role of public forces. He assured that the process of investigation and understanding the border incident continues, with the goal of preserving peace between the neighboring countries. The head of state is personally monitoring the situation, and contacts have been established with RDC authorities.

cg.headline: Lékoumou leads Republic of Congo in 2026 BEPC exam results
cg.dek: The Lékoumou department achieved an 86.57% pass rate, while Congo-Oubangui recorded the lowest at 58.83% among fifteen regions.
paragraphs: The Lékoumou department has emerged as the top performer in the Republic of Congo's 2026 Brevet d’études du premier cycle (BEPC) examinations, with a pass rate of 86.57%. This places it significantly ahead of other regions, including Nkéni-Alima, which secured second place with 77.43%, and Sangha, rounding out the top three at 77.37%. The results offer a snapshot of educational performance across the country's fifteen administrative divisions.

At the lower end of the performance spectrum, the Congo-Oubangui department registered the lowest pass rate at 58.83%. Other departments also showed varying levels of success, with Brazzaville ranking seventh at 70.09% and Pointe-Noire, a major urban center, placing fourteenth with 63.65%. This disparity in results across departments could prompt discussions regarding learning conditions and educational resources.

The ranking highlights a considerable gap in academic achievement between the leading and lagging regions. Lékoumou's performance, with nearly nine out of ten candidates passing, suggests a strong educational framework within the department. This data serves as a key indicator for evaluating territorial educational outcomes and may inform future strategies for pedagogical support and resource allocation.

ci.headline: Abidjan Hosts African Freedom and Development Debate
ci.dek: Think tanks and foundations gathered in Abidjan to discuss rethinking freedom and development based on the continent's realities.
paragraphs: The question of how to rethink freedom and development in Africa, grounded in the continent's human, social, and cultural realities, was central to the "African Freedom Encounters." The event took place on Thursday, September 3, 2026, in Cocody Riviera 4. It was organized by Audace Institut Afrique in partnership with Atlas Network, the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom, and the Center for Research and Action for Peace (Cerap).

The International Book Fair of Abidjan (SILA) also served as a venue for significant political reflection on Thursday, September 3, 2026, in Cocody. This event focused on reinventing democracy in Africa beyond voting, drawing from an essay by Ousmane Ndiaye.

These discussions aimed to foster a deeper understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing the continent in its pursuit of progress and self-determination, bringing together diverse perspectives on governance and societal advancement.

The discussions focused on consolidating the gains achieved so far and exploring the feasibility of prolonging the project's activities. ci.headline: Ivory Coast Basketball Climbs to 35th Globally
ci.dek: The national team gains two spots in the FIBA rankings following strong performances in World Cup qualifiers.
paragraphs: The Ivorian men's national basketball team, known as the Elephants, has advanced two positions to reach 35th place globally in the latest FIBA rankings released in September 2026. This marks an improvement from their previous 37th position in July. The Ivorian Basketball Federation (FIBB) announced the update, attributing the rise to recent successes in international windows, particularly during the 2027 World Cup qualifiers.

With 413.8 points, the team solidifies its position within Africa's top three, building on a record of seven wins and two losses in qualification matches. This climb follows crucial victories against Mali (83-77) and Egypt (72-66) during the fourth qualifying window in Dakar, despite a subsequent loss to Angola (91-70). The team is currently second in Group F with 16 points, trailing Senegal.

The Elephants are well-positioned to secure a spot in the 2027 FIBA World Cup. The final African qualifiers will take place in Abidjan from February 25-28, 2027, at the Palais des sports de Treichville. The national team aims to clinch their qualification in front of their home crowd during this decisive fifth window.

eg.headline: Bus Overturns in South Sinai, Killing 22
eg.dek: A passenger bus carrying Egyptians and Jordanians overturned on the Dahab-Nuweiba road, resulting in 22 fatalities and 28 injuries.
paragraphs: Twenty-two people died and 28 were injured when a passenger bus overturned on the Dahab-Nuweiba road in Egypt’s South Sinai on Wednesday morning. The bus, en route from Cairo to the port of Nuweiba for transit to Jordan, was carrying both Egyptian and Jordanian passengers. The South Sinai governorate stated the vehicle overturned in the Al-Saada area between Dahab and Nuweiba.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has directed the formation of a technical committee to investigate the cause of the crash, examining the vehicle's safety, the driver's condition, and road conditions. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar dispatched 20 ambulances and ordered maximum medical care for the injured, while South Sinai Governor Ismail Mohamed Kamal increased hospital readiness. The Minister of Social Solidarity is coordinating with relief teams for urgent assistance to those affected.

The prime minister expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished a swift recovery for the injured. He also instructed the governor to ensure accurate legal procedures, clear the crash site, and provide necessary support to the victims' families. Medical teams are operating at full capacity to manage the response to the incident.

paragraphs: Russia's defense industry is set to unveil its Su-57E stealth fighter at the Egypt International Airshow 2026, featuring a new suite of armaments. State-owned Rostec will premiere the export-grade variant of the fifth-generation aircraft at the event, scheduled for September 8–10 in El Alamein. The Su-57E will not only be displayed with its newly integrated weapons systems, which have not been publicly exhibited in Russia or elsewhere, but will also conduct live aerial demonstrations.

Alongside the fighter jet's debut, Rostec subsidiary High Precision Systems will present the first foreign demonstration of its "Bison" anti-drone system. This system is designed to intercept and neutralize low-altitude aerial threats and unmanned vehicles. The "Bison" system is being positioned as a key element within Moscow's offerings for defensive systems exports.

The Egypt International Airshow serves as the launchpad for this updated Su-57E variant, highlighting Russia's advancements in military technology for international markets. The event provides a platform for showcasing both offensive and defensive capabilities, with the fighter jet and the anti-drone system representing significant components of Russia's defense export portfolio.

eg.headline: Egypt, IOM Establish Migrant Health Unit
eg.dek: A new agreement between Egypt's Health Ministry and the International Organization for Migration will expand healthcare services for migrants and host communities.
paragraphs: Egypt's Health Ministry will establish a dedicated migrant health unit to oversee healthcare access and coordinate treatment referrals, following an agreement with the International Organization for Migration (IOM). The memorandum of understanding aims to enhance health services for both migrants and host communities. It includes provisions for early HIV detection and treatment, provision of medicines, and field screening campaigns at specialized hospitals, with the IOM covering screening costs.

The partnership also encompasses vaccination campaigns, public health programs, mental health and addiction treatment, and support for blood donation services and national programs targeting respiratory diseases. Deputy Health Minister Amr Kandil and IOM Egypt Chief of Mission Carlos Oliver signed the agreement. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar stated the unit will monitor implementation and coordinate referrals for migrants needing medical care.

The collaboration will also focus on building the capacity of healthcare providers through specialized training courses, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and improving health facility infrastructure. Both sides will work on addressing health challenges related to population pressures and migration flows, including emergency cases, and will establish mechanisms for regular program evaluation. The IOM will provide technical and financial support for healthcare costs and service improvements.

eg.headline: Egypt and China Agree on Middle East Stability
eg.dek: Cairo and Beijing jointly called for a Gaza ceasefire and urged unhindered humanitarian aid delivery into the besieged enclave.
paragraphs: Egypt and China have issued a comprehensive joint statement, reaffirming their commitment to Middle East stability. The declaration specifically calls for a permanent ceasefire in the Gaza Strip and demands the immediate removal of restrictions hindering humanitarian aid delivery. Both nations emphasized the critical need to solidify a lasting peace in the region and advocated for the swift return of the Palestinian Authority to govern Gaza, viewing it as a vital step toward restoring administrative unity and political stability.

The joint statement also expressed severe concern over escalating regional tensions, with both governments condemning the military escalation by Israeli forces in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. They highlighted deep alarm over rising settler violence, systemic land confiscation, and expanding settlement construction, warning that these actions actively undermine peace prospects and emphasized the paramount importance of safeguarding Palestine’s territorial integrity.

Extending their diplomatic posture to North Africa, Egypt and China also called for strict respect for Sudan’s sovereignty, territorial unity, and national institutions. Both powers firmly rejected any external interference in internal Sudanese affairs, underscoring their shared stance on regional security and non-intervention in the domestic matters of other nations.

gq.headline: Government Finalizes Special Economic Zone Law Implementation
gq.dek: A newly sanctioned law aims to boost national growth by establishing special economic zones with fiscal incentives and streamlined procedures.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's government has convened to strategize the implementation of the recently sanctioned Law No. 8/2026, General Law of Special Economic Zones. This legislation is designed to align national development with the Sustainable National Development Strategy (Equatorial Guinea 2035) and the African Union's Agenda 2063. Key aspects include the creation of tax and customs incentives, land leasing schemes, legal guarantees against arbitrary actions, expedited administrative processes, and a consolidated Foreign and Maritime Trade One-Stop Shop.

The government has instructed its technical teams to draft the regulatory framework within an immediate, non-extendable 48-hour deadline. This working group, comprising ministers from Hydrocarbons, Transport, Labor, Finance, Treasury, Justice, Agriculture, Public Works, Land Management, and Economy and Commerce, must present the institutional structure, including statutes and the creation decree for the National Authority of Special Economic Zones. They also need to finalize territorial delimitations for industrial, agro-industrial, logistical, and technological complexes and prepare draft decrees for each priority area.

This accelerated deployment of the foundational law signals the Executive's commitment to fostering a competitive and transparent regulatory environment attractive to global capital. Equatorial Guinea seeks to invigorate key production sectors and position itself as a leading investment destination in the region through modern development instruments. The government has committed to establishing these zones as hubs for investment, production, innovation, and national economic development.

gq.headline: Students Take Extra Exams for University Access
gq.dek: An extraordinary examination session is scheduled for September 23 and 24, offering a chance for students to qualify for university.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's examination commission has set September 23 and 24 for an extraordinary university entrance examination, known as Selectividad. This session is designed for students who did not pass previous tests or have outstanding phases required for university admission. The matriculation process for eligible students began on September 1 and will continue for several days, following the commission's calendar.

This examination is a crucial step for second-year Baccalaureate students aiming to pursue higher education. Meanwhile, secondary schools across the country are currently conducting recovery exams. Students who successfully pass these recovery tests will be eligible to register for the extraordinary Selectividad.

Those who do not succeed in the September extraordinary session will have another opportunity during the ordinary examination period scheduled for June of the following year. The Selectividad tests are a mandatory requirement for entry into university-level studies in the country.

gq.headline: GETESA clarifies account warnings do not mean service suspension
gq.dek: The telecommunications company stated that a system error caused erroneous notifications about account blockages, assuring users their service remains active.
paragraphs: GETESA has assured customers that alerts warning of account blockages are not indicative of actual service suspensions. Several users reported receiving messages stating their accounts would be blocked at 23:59:59 on September 3rd, prompting concern about potential service interruptions. The company clarified that these notifications stem from a temporary issue within the notification system, which is currently being addressed by technical teams.

The erroneous messages, which instructed users to recharge their accounts to avoid blocking, have caused confusion. GETESA emphasized that receiving this alert does not obligate users to make a payment before the specified time to prevent service suspension. The company is actively working on revising and normalizing its notification system to rectify the ongoing incorrect alerts.

GETESA is urging its users to remain calm as the situation is under active management and normalization is in progress. The company's statement aims to alleviate the anxiety caused by the system malfunction and reaffirm the continuity of its services for all affected customers.

gq.headline: GETESA Opens AfriMall Store to Improve Customer Access
gq.dek: The telecommunications company expands its physical presence to offer a wider range of services and better customer support.
paragraphs: GETESA has inaugurated a new store at AfriMall, aiming to bring its services closer to the population. The location will allow customers to manage their mobile lines, including SIM card activation, renewals, replacements, and ownership changes. Additionally, customers can inquire about and subscribe to various internet services, such as TRINET and 4G mobile internet, for both personal and professional use.

The new outlet also stocks essential equipment for these services, including mobile phones from brands like ZTE, Nubia, and Redmi, as well as modems and routers. Standard customer service operations, such as top-ups and service inquiries, will also be available. This opening follows GETESA's recent expansion, including a new store in Malabo in July.

This initiative aligns with the new management's strategy to enhance accessibility and improve the user experience by increasing face-to-face service points. The company views this as part of its ongoing modernization and transformation process, aiming to facilitate customer interactions and streamline service administration.

gq.headline: Grand Hotel Djibloho Offers Tourism Package
gq.dek: The hotel's World Tourism Day promotion combines accommodation, dining, leisure, and excursions for groups.
paragraphs: El Grand Hotel Djibloho has launched a special weekend package to promote national tourism, coinciding with World Tourism Day. The initiative offers a comprehensive experience including round-trip transport from Bata, two nights' accommodation with breakfast, and a special "Taste of the World" dinner. This package aims to showcase Djibloho's attractions by integrating various elements into a single offering.

The program also features an outdoor Afro Fitness session and an excursion to Ndong Mba and Malamba, designed to immerse participants in the local culture and natural environment. Entertainment is provided through a White Party at Ozean Pool Bar, complete with live music and a DJ. This multi-faceted approach seeks to provide a memorable national tourism experience.

This special offer is available for groups of at least 10 people. Pricing is set at 205,000 XAF per person for single occupancy and 290,000 XAF for double occupancy. Reservations and further information can be obtained via WhatsApp at +240 555 502 359. The hotel is promoting domestic travel through this curated weekend getaway.

er.headline: Eritrean Community in Egypt Marks Independence Struggle Anniversary
er.dek: Nationals in Cairo gathered to commemorate the 65th anniversary of the armed struggle for Eritrean independence with cultural displays.
paragraphs: The Eritrean community residing in Egypt held a patriotic celebration in Cairo to mark the 65th anniversary of the commencement of the armed struggle for Eritrean independence. The event, which took place on September 1, featured cultural programs designed to reflect the significance of Bahti Meskerem for the Eritrean people.

Mr. Aman Abdelwasi’e, the Charge d’Affaires at the Eritrean Embassy, addressed attendees, emphasizing September 1 as a pivotal date in the nation's history. He stated that the day signifies the beginning of the armed struggle for independence and dignity, serving as a reminder for citizens to intensify their efforts in national development initiatives.

The celebration underscored the importance of the armed struggle in Eritrea's journey toward self-determination and highlighted its ongoing relevance to national progress. The gathering provided a platform for the Eritrean diaspora in Egypt to connect with their heritage and reaffirm their commitment to the country's development.

ke.headline: Milk Shortage Empties Shelves, Raises Prices for Kenyan Consumers
ke.dek: Supermarket supplies dwindle and prices climb as drought and rising feed costs impact dairy production across the nation.
paragraphs: Kenya is experiencing a significant milk shortage, leading to empty supermarket shelves, rationing, and increased prices for consumers. The scarcity, which has been noticeable for about a week, is particularly affecting urban areas where milky tea, or chai, is a daily staple. Restaurants are struggling to meet demand, with owners reporting difficulties in sourcing even small quantities of milk. This situation is impacting daily routines and social customs that often involve the consumption of chai.

The government attributes the milk deficit to drought conditions that have reduced pasture availability. However, the industry regulator acknowledges "supply constraints" and "low stock levels." The Consumer Federation of Kenya (Cofek) points to delayed seasonal rains and a 45% increase in animal feed costs as primary drivers. Cofek also suggests that the dairy sector failed to adequately manage last year's milk surplus, which could have been processed into powder to mitigate current shortages.

Formal milk deliveries to processors saw a 3.7% decrease from June to July, with further declines expected in August, according to the Kenya Dairy Board. Fresh milk prices have risen from 70 to 80 Kenyan shillings per liter. Cofek stated that the shortage was foreseeable and largely avoidable, criticizing the lack of proactive measures to manage surplus milk production from the previous year.

ke.headline: Kenyan Farmers Aggregate Livestock for Stronger Market Power
ke.dek: Pastoralists in Isiolo are combining herds to attract buyers and secure better prices, shifting from viewing animals as symbols of wealth to commercial assets.
paragraphs: Muhamed Hayota Dadable, a 43-year-old farmer from Isiolo, now understands the value of aggregating livestock, a lesson learned too late during a devastating 2010 drought that wiped out his animals. He joined the Nasole Cooperative five years ago, inspired by his wife's savings and access to loans, which helped him pay for his daughter's high school admission. This shift in perspective, from viewing livestock as mere wealth to commercial assets, is being fostered by the Kenya Livestock Marketing and Resilience (KLMP) Program, implemented by Heifer International.

The KLMP Program, funded by the Swedish Embassy and operating in Isiolo, Samburu, Laikipia, Kajiado, and Nakuru counties, aims to strengthen red meat production and marketing. Heifer International facilitates partnerships, connecting farmers with businesses and service providers. Through livestock aggregation, farmers combine their animals, creating larger, more attractive herds for buyers. This collective approach, where individual small herds are merged into groups of around 250, significantly enhances their bargaining power.

This new strategy allows farmers to capture more value from their animals. By pooling resources, pastoralists can negotiate better terms and prices than they could individually. This method transforms how livestock is managed, moving towards a more commercial and resilient approach to pastoralism, offering a crucial buffer against the uncertainties of drought and market fluctuations.

ke.headline: President Orders Tata Chemicals to Exit Kenya
ke.dek: Kenya's president has ordered Tata Chemicals to cease operations, citing a failure to sufficiently benefit the nation and a preference for exporting raw materials.
paragraphs: President William Ruto has directed Tata Chemicals to leave Kenya, stating the company has not generated adequate benefits for the country. The factory, located in Magadi, is Africa's leading producer of natural soda ash. Ruto expressed dissatisfaction with the company's practice of exporting soda ash instead of processing it locally into products like glass and chemicals.

The government plans to bring in new investors to take over the operations at Lake Magadi, with the stated aim of increasing employment and investment opportunities for Kenyans. Tata Chemicals, part of India's Tata Group, has operated in Kenya for nearly a century, exporting over 350,000 tonnes of soda ash annually to various international markets.

Tata Chemicals stated it respects the government's decision and is committed to resolving outstanding matters through appropriate legal and regulatory channels. The announcement was made by President Ruto during a visit to Kajiado county, where the company's plant is situated. The company's continued operation has been a subject of recent developments.

ke.headline: Police Chief Orders Probe Into Journalist Abduction
ke.dek: Inspector General Douglas Kanja has ordered investigations into the alleged kidnapping of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich in Gilgil.
paragraphs: The National Police Service has launched an investigation into the alleged abduction of Standard Group Associate Editor Alex Kiprotich. Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja ordered the probe after reports surfaced that Kiprotich was kidnapped on Tuesday in Gilgil. The police service stated that kidnapping and abduction are treated with utmost seriousness, posing threats to the lives, liberty, and security of Kenyans. The Anti-Abduction Unit has taken up the case to identify those responsible and bring them to justice.

NPS spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga confirmed the Inspector General's directive, emphasizing the need to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Nyaga noted that heavily armed individuals were reportedly seen ordering occupants out of their vehicle. The police service unequivocally condemned any act of kidnapping, abduction, or intimidation that interferes with press freedom or other constitutional rights, assuring the public of a transparent investigation.

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has also called for an immediate investigation into the alleged abduction. CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal described the incident as a "shameful indictment" of the Kenya Kwanza administration and raised concerns about journalist safety and press freedom. The New York-based organization expressed worry over an escalation in abduction and enforced disappearance cases in Kenya.

ke.headline: Nairobi Nurses Protest Government Labor Grievances
ke.dek: Dozens of nurses marched in Nairobi, demanding action on a collective bargaining agreement and protesting a strike that has entered its 37th day.
paragraphs: Nurses in Nairobi took to the streets wearing white and carrying placards to protest the government's alleged failure to address labor grievances. The demonstration comes as a strike, which began in late July, continues to affect public health facilities nationwide.

Seth Panayko, Secretary-General of the Kenya National Union of Nurses, stated that pushback between the Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC) and the Council of Governors has persisted since 2017. He indicated the nurses' intention to visit the SRC to request a letter of no objection for their Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA).

Collins Otieno Ajwang, president of the National Nurses Association, expressed concern over the strike's impact on patients, noting that the continuing delay is costing both patients and the healthcare system. Joseph Chebii, secretary general for clinical officers associations, urged all stakeholders, including unions and government bodies, to engage in discussions to resolve the issue and prevent further losses.

za.headline: Sharpeville survivors challenge apartheid-era law blocking compensation
za.dek: Legal action seeks to overturn legislation preventing claims for damages from the 1960 massacre, aiming for government dialogue on reparations.
paragraphs: Lawyers representing survivors and relatives of those killed in the 1960 Sharpeville Massacre have initiated legal proceedings against the South African government. The action targets a law enacted shortly after the event that has barred compensation claims for over sixty years. The Sharpeville Massacre, where police fired on protesters, resulted in 69 deaths and at least 180 injuries according to official records, becoming a stark symbol of apartheid's brutality.

The legal challenge, spearheaded by Lawyers for Human Rights, aims to open a dialogue with the government regarding reparations for victims and their families. Survivors like 87-year-old Abram Mofokeng, who was shot in the foot and back, and Mpai Chabane, whose grandmother was killed, express deep emotional and financial hardship. They seek justice through compensation and the preservation of the township's history, which is slowly falling into disrepair.

The Sharpeville Massacre occurred on March 21, 1960, as protesters demonstrated against pass laws that restricted the movement of Black South Africans. While official figures state 69 killed and 180 wounded, subsequent research cited by lawyers suggests at least 91 people died and over 238 were injured. The day of the massacre is now observed as Human Rights Day, a public holiday, following the end of apartheid.

za.headline: Zungu Challenges Incumbent Jordaan for Safa Presidency
za.dek: AmaZulu owner Sandile Zungu faces Danny Jordaan, who is seeking a fourth term as Safa president despite ongoing fraud charges.
paragraphs: Businessman Sandile Zungu is challenging Danny Jordaan for the South African Football Association (Safa) presidency at the upcoming elective congress on September 12. Jordaan, who has led Safa since 2013, is seeking a fourth term despite facing ongoing fraud charges. Zungu, owner of the AmaZulu football club, has received the backing of AmaZulu King Misuzulu kaZwelithini, who urged all 11 KwaZulu-Natal football regions to support his bid.

Jordaan, who turned 75 on September 3, has been president of Safa since replacing Kirsten Nematandani. He has faced challengers before and is currently serving his third term. His arrest in November 2024 for fraud, along with Safa's chief of finance and former CEO, has led to calls for his resignation, but Safa's constitution does not mandate this. The fraud case remains in the pre-trial phase.

Despite the legal proceedings, Jordaan remains confident in his re-election, attributing the accusations to a coordinated attack by critics within Safa. He believes such campaigns are intended to deter sponsors, noting that football is uniquely targeted compared to rugby and cricket. Zungu's candidacy presents a significant challenge to Jordaan's long tenure at the helm of South African football.

za.headline: Diesel Prices Jump 62% Amid Strait of Hormuz Conflict
za.dek: South African diesel double-cab owners face significantly higher refueling costs due to a 62% price increase since January.
paragraphs: Diesel prices for 50 ppm fuel have surged by 62% since January 2026, with the latest increase on September 2 pushing the coast price to R28.79 per litre and inland to R30.05 per litre. This escalation, driven by events in the Strait of Hormuz, has added R11.03 per litre coast and R11.53 per litre inland. The conflict, triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, led Iran to close the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil transit route.

Filling an 80-litre tank now costs R2,303.20 on the coast and R2,404.00 inland, an increase of R882.40 and R922.40 respectively compared to January. This means motorists may spend nearly R900 more per fill-up, with many refilling weekly. The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources and National Treasury have not implemented fuel levy reductions or other safeguards to mitigate these costs.

Analysts do not expect Middle East oil production to normalize before early 2027, suggesting continued high fuel costs. The relative strength of the rand has partially offset the price hikes, preventing even more severe increases. Owners of diesel double-cab bakkies are being advised to consider alternatives like petrol or new-energy vehicles.
